beat: round one: question, four answers, four star reactions (cut line and exit noted only where they bear on the round's shape)
lineCountNote: 8 episodes x 9 lines (1 question, 4 answers, 4 reactions) = 72 lines. 28 flagged = 39%. Split: answers 7 of 32 flagged (22%), reactions 18 of 32 flagged (56%), questions 2 of 8. The answers are near the bar; the reactions are not.

headToHead.ours: Tilly (script-r1/ep-06): "You're completely right, and I've been trained to say that to people who aren't."
headToHead.bar: Vera #12: "Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!"
headToHead.verdict: Tie on the line. Same fake-out-then-blade shape, and Tilly's is better built to her persona. But Vesper answers it with "Another headset on my air, Tilly. It's been a while.", which ignores it. In Monster Prom the line is the end of the beat; here the star steps on it with a non-reaction. Bar wins on the moment.

headToHead.ours: Crumb (script-r1/ep-05): "Dash. I watched him A/B test two bananas. He shipped the brown one." then Maximilian: "We do not tidy our colleagues in public."
headToHead.bar: Rival player options #78: "Haven't you heard, Scott? Fishsticks make you worse at sports!..." and the rival undercut structure (A claims, B states the plain fact).
headToHead.verdict: Ours. A rival's logic used against him, ending on the turn word, and a star reply that actually answers it. The one round in the batch that works like the bar, because the question forces suitors to name each other. But Dash answers two lines later and never hits back at Crumb, so the rivalry dies on the spot.

headToHead.ours: Maximilian to Nav (script-r1/ep-02): "I have fourteen chauffeurs. I am sacking thirteen." after Nav: "They muted me at a junction, so I left them at it."
headToHead.bar: Narrator #63: "It is just paper!" / #58 "Does... Scott know any other people? Signs are pointing to "no.""
headToHead.verdict: Close to the bar: the star's status move and the undercut in two short sentences. But it is charmed while sounding like a threat, and every other reaction in that round is charmed too, so the line has nothing to stand against. Bar edges it.

headToHead.ours: Nav (script-r1/ep-01): "You are a small blue dot, facing the wrong way. Turn around. There. Me."
headToHead.bar: Liam/player #30: "3.85 billion BC, so you can be into existing before it was cool." (escalation by literalism)
headToHead.verdict: Comparable. The bot's interface taken literally and turned into a pick-up line, with the turn on the last word. Star reply "Said like a forecast, and for once I believed it" is the wrong machine (weather, not satnav) and a stock phrase. Bar wins on the exchange.

headToHead.ours: Dash (script-r1/ep-03): "Private jet! Okay, jet's a stretch. Private bus. Private seat. I'll save you a seat on the bus."
headToHead.bar: Damien #19 denial-then-reveal; Valerie #87 deadpan shop blurbs.
headToHead.verdict: Ours holds as a line: a live pivot down a funnel, in Dash's logic. Vesper's reply "I'm not cutting to the news, Dash, let it run" is generic radio patter that any answer would get. Bar wins on the exchange.

headToHead.ours: Structure: a full round, e.g. script-r1/ep-02 (four answers on 'how did your last relationship end', four 'charmed' reactions, four-way tie at 3, cut by tiebreak).
headToHead.bar: The Dating Game (one question, several answers, the chooser follows up) and Take Me Out (lights go off in visible waves; the host asks the women why).
headToHead.verdict: Bar, clearly. In the real formats each answer moves the board where you can see it, and the 'why' is said about the answer just given. Ours reads four unrelated answers in sequence. Only one round in eight (ep-05) has a suitor react to another suitor. Reactions follow the card hit, not the line, so viewers watching window A cannot read who is winning from what was said.

biggestGap: Star reactions are chosen by which card an answer hit, or by the suitor's persona and costume, not by what the answer said: 18 of 32 round-one reactions miss the line just spoken (Brock 'very quietly' gets 'Don't shout at me'; Crumb's sourdough gets 'That ding went out live'; Tilly's best line gets 'Another headset on my air'). Monster Prom's narrator and the Dating Game chooser win because the undercut is about the exact line before it. Fix: author each round-one answer with its own star replies, one warm and one cold per star (3 stars x 2), keyed to that answer's id; the selector picks the reply that matches the card sentiment and falls back to card-generic reactions only when none exists.
pickMakesSense: Round-one cuts are legible in 5 of 8: ep-01 Brock, ep-04 Crumb, ep-05 Dash, ep-06 Quill, hybrid-01 Crumb, though hybrid-01 has no favourite because all four go negative. They are not legible in 3: ep-02 is a four-way tie at 3, all charmed, decided by a hidden tiebreak, and Nav gets cut straight after Maximilian's warmest reaction. ep-03 cuts Crumb on a cringe with no card behind it, after the strongest answer of the round. hybrid-02 cuts Brock for the sincerest answer, through a reaction that misreads it.
structuralChange: Make answer 4 a reply, not a cold answer. After the star reacts to answer 3, the fourth suitor speaks to the current leader's answer (the highest standing so far, or any suitor who named them): a steal or undercut of 14 words or fewer, from a per-rival-pair bank. The round-two [jab] bank already holds most of these. Then the star gives one 10-word reaction that settles the comparison, then the cut. No new line is added, so the timing stays the same. It guarantees one build per round, sets up a visible favourite and a suitor in trouble before window B opens, and copies the one round that works (script-r1/ep-05, where Crumb names Dash). Also, under the same selection logic: never draw a round-one question whose natural answers hit a hidden card for all four suitors (script-r1/ep-02).
